boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UCLA spaces for quiet work, collaboration, and low-key campus activity, each supported by a direct UCLA or UCLA-affiliated source.

cards.title: Settle into Powell’s Main Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Powell Library
cards.notes: Bring a reading-heavy task and use the quiet second-floor room; the library lists it as a study space with access to Powell Community Collections.
cards.short_summary: A quiet historic-library room for focused reading and coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Library identifies the Powell Main Reading Room as a quiet study space on Powell Library’s second floor.
cards.access_notes: Check the Powell Library page for current building hours and access details.

cards.title: Use the Rose Gilbert Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Powell Library
cards.notes: Choose a chair or couch past the Rotunda for individual reading; the room includes popular magazines and journals alongside its quiet study setting.
cards.short_summary: A quieter Powell option with lounge-style seating and current periodicals.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Library describes the Rose Gilbert Reading Room as a quiet second-floor space with chairs, couches, magazines, and journals.
cards.access_notes: Located past the Rotunda; confirm Powell Library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Reserve a Powell group study room
cards.subtitle: First floor, Powell Library
cards.notes: Plan a small project meeting and reserve a room near the first-floor reading room; each has seating, power, and a display screen for collaboration.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms designed for small-team project work.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Library says Powell’s six group study rooms support up to eight people and include seating, power outlets, and a screen.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required; consult UCLA Library’s current reservation process and room availability.

cards.title: Huddle in a YRL collaboration pod
cards.subtitle: First-floor Research Commons, Young Research Library
cards.notes: Reserve a pod when your group needs a shared screen and table; the first-floor Research Commons has twenty pods seating six to eight people.
cards.short_summary: Screen-equipped group pods in YRL’s flexible research hub.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Library lists twenty YRL Collaboration Pods in the first-floor Research Commons, each seating six to eight people with LCD screens.
cards.source_title: Charles E. Young Research Library | UCLA Library
cards.access_notes: Pods are reservable; verify availability and Research Library hours before going.

cards.title: Work from YRL’s Garden Commons
cards.subtitle: A-level, Young Research Library
cards.notes: Use this A-level study area when you need power and a printer nearby; UCLA Library also lists maps and microform in the Garden Commons.
cards.short_summary: A library study zone with practical research and printing resources.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Library states that YRL’s Garden Commons includes study spaces with power outlets, a printer, maps, and microform.
cards.source_title: Charles E. Young Research Library | UCLA Library
cards.access_notes: Located on YRL’s A-level; consult current Research Library hours.

cards.entity_name: Biomedical Library Collaboration Hub Study Rooms
cards.title: Book a Biomedical Library Collaboration Hub room
cards.subtitle: Room 22-001, Louise M. Darling Biomedical Library
cards.notes: Reserve one of the sixth-floor rooms for a focused small-group session; all eight rooms are intended for group use, not solo studying.
cards.short_summary: Eight reservable group rooms in UCLA’s biomedical library.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Library says the Biomedical Library Collaboration Hub has eight sixth-floor study rooms, all intended for group use only.
cards.source_title: Louise M. Darling Biomedical Library | UCLA Library
cards.access_notes: Rooms are in 22-001 and require reservation; check library hours and current policies.

cards.title: Meet in the SEL Research Commons
cards.subtitle: 8251 Boelter Hall, Science and Engineering Library
cards.notes: Use the Boelter-based commons for a collaborative work block or STEM learning activity; it provides group collaboration space to the UCLA community.
cards.short_summary: A STEM-oriented collaboration space within Boelter Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Library identifies the SEL Research Commons in 8251 Boelter Hall as group collaboration space and home to the STEM Collaborative Learning Center.
cards.source_title: Science and Engineering Library | UCLA Library
cards.access_notes: Check Science and Engineering Library hours and any study-space reservation requirements.

cards.entity_name: Arts Library Quiet Study Reading Room
cards.title: Find a carrel in the Arts Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Fifth floor, Arts Library
cards.notes: Head to the fifth floor for a quiet independent-work session; choose among individual carrels, tables, and varied seating in the reading room.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet room above the Arts Library’s main floor.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Library describes the fifth-floor Arts Library Quiet Study Reading Room as reserved for quiet study with carrels, tables, and varied seating.
cards.access_notes: The reading room is reserved for quiet study; verify Arts Library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Pause among the Murphy Sculpture Garden works
cards.subtitle: North campus, adjacent to Young Research Library
cards.notes: Walk the formal plaza, coral-tree path, and sloping lawn at an unhurried pace; informal seating and lawns were designed for pausing and reflection.
cards.short_summary: A five-acre outdoor UCLA art setting with more than 70 sculptures.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hammer Museum says the garden spans more than five acres of UCLA campus, holds over 70 sculptures, and includes seating and lawns intended for reflection.
cards.source_title: Franklin D. Murphy Sculpture Garden | Hammer Museum
cards.access_notes: The Hammer Museum places the garden on UCLA campus; tours can be scheduled through its tours information.

cards.title: Play a low-key game at Mapes Beach
cards.subtitle: Sunset Canyon Recreation Center
cards.notes: Bring your own volleyball and use an open-recreation court when available; the facility has three regulation sand courts plus one practice court.
cards.short_summary: Sand volleyball courts for UCLA recreation and organized play.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Recreation states that Mapes Beach has three regulation sand courts and one practice court, with open-recreation use first come, first served.
cards.source_title: Sunset Canyon Recreation Center | UCLA Recreation
cards.access_notes: Open recreation is first come, first served; users bring equipment and should check current hours or reservations.
